items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: 21 of 25 ACs bound within the two declared roots (plugins/shipwright-project/tests, shared/tests); the remaining 4 recorded unbound with concrete reasons (2 root-flagged via trg-704cdb22, 2 genuinely un-instructed); shipwright_ac_coverage_baseline.json regenerated via check_ac_coverage_ratchet.py --write; one pytest invocation per root planned for F0.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: Test-only diff (plus two pyproject.toml marker registrations); no new runtime error paths introduced.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No new inputs, auth surfaces, or secrets; diff is tests + doc-reading assertions + a marker registration + a regenerated coverage baseline.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: Each binding traced to the real code path proving the AC (pure GateResult functions, or the specific grill-trace STOP check), not a renderer/pin-only or gameable-proxy shape. External code review caught one wrapper-only binding (FR-01.02/AC07) and one mislabeled tag (FR-01.16/AC10 on the wrong test) -- both fixed before finalization by pairing the pure-function test and dropping the mislabel.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: New tests follow the existing test_<behavior> naming convention in each file; no dead code, no unused imports; three new test files stayed under the 300-line bloat-gate cap (checked explicitly for every touched/new file).

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: shipwright_ac_coverage_baseline.json is a producer(check_ac_coverage_ratchet.py --write)/consumer(the same script, read-only, plus CI's gate) boundary. Round-trip probe run: wrote the baseline from a freshly-regenerated manifest, then re-ran the read-only gate against the same manifest and confirmed status=clean with zero new_unbound -- the write and the read agree.
